ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The yellow shaded part in the figure is an almost complete circle. A wedge-shaped “mouth” has been cut off on the right side. This gap is enclosed by two straight radius boundaries starting from the center of the circle and the missing arc on the circumference; the 1 marked in the figure indicates that the radius of the circle is 1 cm, and the 60° marked next to the gap indicates that the central angle of the mouth is 60°. Reasoning: The entire circumference corresponds to 360°, and the gap is 60°, so the arc retained on the outside of the monster corresponds to 360° - 60° = 300°. The radius r=1 cm, therefore the retained arc length is (300/360)·2π·1 = 5π/3. The perimeter of the monster also includes the two straight sides of the mouth, each of which is a radius, with lengths 1 cm and 1 cm respectively. The total perimeter is 5π/3 + 1 + 1 = 5π/3 + 2.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the yellow monster is almost a full circle with a wedge-shaped mouth cut out on the right; the two sides of the mouth are straight radius segments from the center to the circle, and the label 1 indicates the circle radius. From the text, use radius r=1 cm and missing mouth central angle 60°. The shaded boundary is a 300° major arc plus the two radius sides of the mouth. Compute the arc length as (300/360)·2π·1 = 5π/3, then add the two straight sides 1+1. The perimeter is 5π/3 + 2.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the figure is a full circle except for a 60° wedge removed on the right, creating two straight exposed mouth edges; the radius is shown as 1. From the text, take r=1 cm and the cut-out angle as 60°. Start with the circumference of the full circle, 2πr = 2π. The removed mouth would have contributed only the small circular arc of angle 60°, whose length is (60/360)·2π·1 = π/3; subtract this missing arc from the full circumference. Then add the two new straight boundary edges of the mouth, each equal to the radius 1. Thus the perimeter is 2π - π/3 + 2 = 5π/3 + 2.
